key_insight: For pulmonary embolism risk stratification, tabular medical records and cardiac biomarkers outperformed vascular features, and even graph neural networks on CTPA-derived vascular graphs did not add clear value.
clinical_relevance: This suggests that, in routine PE triage, readily available clinical data may be more useful than complex vascular graph modeling when blood tests or richer imaging features are missing.
method: Benchmarked tabular models using medical records and cardiac biomarkers.
Added vascular biomarkers extracted from CTPA to assess incremental benefit.
Applied graph neural networks to the pulmonary vascular tree's intrinsic graph representation.
evidence_signal: The study used a private dataset of 353 PE cases with complete risk-stratification data and found no performance gain from vascular biomarkers or vascular-graph GNNs over strong global-feature baselines.
watch_item: The dataset is small and private, so the negative finding may not fully generalize across scanners, hospitals, or broader PE populations.
paper_title: Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification from CTPA and Medical Records: Vascular Graphs Are Not All You Need
